views.name: superhero_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero

params.description: One-row-per-superhero core entity view providing basic identifying and physical attributes for each superhero.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve a list of superheroes with their names, identifiers, and physical attributes (height, weight). | Serve as the canonical base when composing additional joins to enrich superhero attributes (publisher, gender, alignment, race, colours) while preserving one-row-per-superhero semantics. | Filter or group-by individual superheroes (e.g., find superheroes taller than X cm, or average weight by publisher) before joining to one-to-many detail tables.
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier for the superhero. Derived from superhero.id. | superhero_name: The public or hero name of the superhero. Derived from superhero.superhero_name. | full_name: The civilian or real full name of the superhero. Derived from superhero.full_name. | gender_id: Foreign key identifier referencing the superhero's gender. Derived from superhero.gender_id. | publisher_id: Foreign key identifier referencing the publisher (e.g., Marvel, DC). Derived from superhero.publisher_id. | alignment_id: Foreign key identifier referencing moral alignment (e.g., hero, villain). Derived from superhero.alignment_id. | race_id: Foreign key identifier referencing race/species. Derived from superhero.race_id. | eye_colour_id: Foreign key identifier for eye colour. Derived from superhero.eye_colour_id. | hair_colour_id: Foreign key identifier for hair colour. Derived from superhero.hair_colour_id. | skin_colour_id: Foreign key identifier for skin colour. Derived from superhero.skin_colour_id. | height_cm: Height of the superhero in centimetres. Derived from superhero.height_cm. | weight_kg: Weight of the superhero in kilograms. Derived from superhero.weight_kg.
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.full_name | superhero.gender_id | superhero.publisher_id | superhero.alignment_id | superhero.race_id | superhero.eye_colour_id | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | superhero.height_cm | superhero.weight_kg
params.metric: id = superhero.id | superhero_name = superhero.superhero_name | full_name = superhero.full_name | gender_id = superhero.gender_id | publisher_id = superhero.publisher_id | alignment_id = superhero.alignment_id | race_id = superhero.race_id | eye_colour_id = superhero.eye_colour_id | hair_colour_id = superhero.hair_colour_id | skin_colour_id = superhero.skin_colour_id | height_cm = superhero.height_cm | weight_kg = superhero.weight_kg
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-to-one (or many-to-one from this view) on the foreign key columns without re-aggregation. Examples: |   - join to gender on superhero_basic.gender_id = gender.id — safe because superhero_basic is one row per superhero and gender is one row per gender; joining will not duplicate superhero rows. |   - join to publisher on superhero_basic.publisher_id = publisher.id — safe for same reason; publisher is one row per publisher. |   - join to alignment on superhero_basic.alignment_id = alignment.id — safe. |   - join to race on superhero_basic.race_id = race.id — safe. |   - join to colour lookup tables (eye_colour, hair_colour, skin_colour) on the respective _id columns — safe. | Do NOT directly join superhero_basic to one-to-many detail tables (for example: superhero_powers, appearances, issues, teammates) without aggregation, because these joins will multiply superhero_basic rows and therefore duplicate any measures derived at the superhero grain. Instead: |   - to attach aggregated info from a one-to-many table, first aggregate at superhero.id in that table (e.g., COUNT(*) AS power_count GROUP BY superhero_id) and then join the aggregated result to superhero_basic on superhero_basic.id = aggregated.superhero_id. |   - alternatively, join and then re-aggregate at superhero.id to restore one-row-per-superhero semantics. | When composing metrics (averages, sums) from this view, treat it as pre-aggregated at the superhero grain. Aggregations across superheroes (e.g., AVG(height_cm) GROUP BY publisher_id) are safe; aggregations that mix child-row-level metrics without re-aggregation are not.

views.name: hero_power_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_id AS hero_id,
  power_id AS power_id
FROM hero_power

params.description: Lists which powers are assigned to which heroes — a mapping of hero_id to power_id (many-to-many link table view).
params.when_to_use: Find all powers for a given hero (e.g., list power_ids for hero_id = X). | Find all heroes that have a given power (e.g., list hero_ids for power_id = Y). | Use as a joinable linking layer when composing hero <-> power relationships in higher-level queries (e.g., count powers per hero, count heroes per power). | Filter or restrict analyses to only heroes that have any of a set of powers or only powers assigned to a set of heroes.
params.output_schema: hero_id: identifier of the hero — derives from hero_power.hero_id | power_id: identifier of the power — derives from hero_power.power_id
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts rows in this view (each row represents one hero_id/power_id association) | distinct_hero_count = COUNT(DISTINCT hero_id)  -- number of unique heroes present in hero_power | distinct_power_count = COUNT(DISTINCT power_id)  -- number of unique powers present in hero_power | powers_per_hero(hero_id) = COUNT(power_id) GROUP BY hero_id  -- aggregate definition to get number of powers assigned to each hero | heroes_per_power(power_id) = COUNT(hero_id) GROUP BY power_id  -- aggregate definition to get number of heroes assigned to each power
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to superhero_basic on hero_id — safe because superhero_basic is a normalization/view keyed 1:1 (or 1:0..1) per hero_id so joining will not duplicate link rows; use LEFT JOIN superhero_basic ON hero_id = superhero_basic.hero_id to enrich link rows with hero attributes without changing counts per hero_id/power_id pair. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension table that is 1:1 per power_id (e.g., a power dimension view) on power_id — safe because the dimension provides at most one row per power_id and will not duplicate link rows. | do NOT join directly to a table/view that is one-to-many from hero_id (for example another table that lists many events per hero) without re-aggregating first — such a join would multiply the hero_id/power_id rows and therefore multiply any measures derived from this view (e.g., row_count or powers_per_hero) unless you pre-aggregate the many-side to one row per hero_id (or per hero_id/power_id as appropriate). | when needing counts after joining to a many-side, either: (a) aggregate the many-side to one row per join key before joining, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate using COUNT(DISTINCT hero_id, power_id) or GROUP BY hero_id/power_id as appropriate to remove duplication. | example safe composition patterns: (1) to get power details for each link: SELECT hpl.hero_id, hpl.power_id, p.name FROM hero_power_link hpl JOIN power_dim p ON hpl.power_id = p.power_id; (2) to get count of powers per hero: SELECT hpl.hero_id, COUNT(hpl.power_id) AS powers_per_hero FROM hero_power_link hpl GROUP BY hpl.hero_id. | example unsafe composition to avoid without re-aggregation: SELECT hpl.hero_id, COUNT(*) FROM hero_power_link hpl JOIN hero_events e ON hpl.hero_id = e.hero_id GROUP BY hpl.hero_id;  -- unsafe because events are many-per-hero and will inflate counts unless you deduplicate or aggregate events first.

views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  power_name
FROM
  superpower

params.description: Lookup of superpower identifiers to canonical power names (one row per superpower).
params.when_to_use: Translate a superpower id to its human-readable name in SELECTs or JOINs. | Filter or group queries by power_name or id when analyzing superheroes and their powers. | Compose into other views that need superpower metadata (e.g., counts of heroes per power) as a dimensional lookup.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for a superpower — derives from base column superpower.id | power_name: canonical name/label of the superpower — derives from base column superpower.power_name
params.metric: id = superpower.id | power_name = superpower.power_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to superhero_basic on hero_power_link.superhero_id = superhero_basic.id via hero_power_link (JOIN) — safe because superpower_lookup is one-row-per-superpower and joins through hero_power_link (a junction) will not duplicate superpower_lookup's rows if you join on superpower id and then aggregate on superhero_basic or hero_power_link side. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join directly to hero_power_link on superpower_lookup.id = hero_power_link.superpower_id — safe as a dimensional join when the query aggregates measures from hero_power_link or superhero_basic afterwards; superpower_lookup itself contains no aggregatable measures so its rows won't introduce duplication of metrics, but measures from hero_power_link are many-per-superpower and must be aggregated appropriately. | do NOT join to one-to-many tables/views (for example joining superpower_lookup directly to hero_power_link and selecting aggregated measures from hero_power_link without GROUP BY on superpower_lookup.id) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side first, because that would multiply counts/sums sourced from the many-side. | When composing metrics: if you need counts of heroes per power, first aggregate hero_power_link (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT hero_id) AS hero_count GROUP BY superpower_id) and then join that aggregated result to superpower_lookup on id to avoid row duplication. | Safe pattern example: SELECT sp.id, sp.power_name, hp.hero_count FROM superpower_lookup sp LEFT JOIN (SELECT superpower_id, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM hero_power_link GROUP BY superpower_id) hp ON sp.id = hp.superpower_id — this preserves one-row-per-superpower and avoids duplicating measures. | Unsafe pattern to avoid: SELECT sp.id, sp.power_name, COUNT(hpl.hero_id) FROM superpower_lookup sp JOIN hero_power_link hpl ON sp.id = hpl.superpower_id; without GROUP BY sp.id this will return an incorrect single-row aggregation or duplicate sp rows when combined with other joins.

SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,

params.description: Provides one-row-per-superhero core attributes (identifiers and basic physical/demographic fields) for use as a foundational building block in larger queries.
params.when_to_use: Look up basic attributes for a specific superhero by id or name | Filter or group analyses by demographic or physical attributes (gender, race, publisher, alignment, colours) | Compose into analytics that need a stable one-row-per-superhero seed (e.g., count of heroes by publisher with joins to power tables) | Join to dimension/look-up tables to enrich labels for id-coded attributes | Use as the left side of joins when you need to preserve one row per superhero
params.output_schema: id: surrogate primary key for the superhero. Derived from table superhero.id | superhero_name: the public/stage name of the hero. Derived from superhero.superhero_name | full_name: the hero's real/full name. Derived from superhero.full_name | gender_id: foreign-key id referencing the hero's gender. Derived from superhero.gender_id | eye_colour_id: foreign-key id for eye colour. Derived from superhero.eye_colour_id | hair_colour_id: foreign-key id for hair colour. Derived from superhero.hair_colour_id | skin_colour_id: foreign-key id for skin colour. Derived from superhero.skin_colour_id | race_id: foreign-key id for race. Derived from superhero.race_id | publisher_id: foreign-key id for publisher/brand. Derived from superhero.publisher_id | alignment_id: foreign-key id for moral alignment. Derived from superhero.alignment_id | height_cm: numeric height in centimetres. Derived from superhero.height_cm | weight_kg: numeric weight in kilograms. Derived from superhero.weight_kg
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.full_name | superhero.gender_id | superhero.eye_colour_id | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | superhero.race_id | superhero.publisher_id | superhero.alignment_id | superhero.height_cm | superhero.weight_kg
params.metric: id = superhero.id | superhero_name = superhero.superhero_name | full_name = superhero.full_name | gender_id = superhero.gender_id | eye_colour_id = superhero.eye_colour_id | hair_colour_id = superhero.hair_colour_id | skin_colour_id = superhero.skin_colour_id | race_id = superhero.race_id | publisher_id = superhero.publisher_id | alignment_id = superhero.alignment_id | height_cm = superhero.height_cm | weight_kg = superhero.weight_kg
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/look-up views/tables (e.g., gender lookup, publisher lookup, alignment lookup, colour lookup) on the corresponding id columns (e.g., superhero_core.gender_id = gender_lookup.id). Safe because those lookups are expected to be one-row-per-id, so joining will not duplicate superhero_core rows or its measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to superhero_basic (sibling NORM) on id (superhero_core.id = superhero_basic.id). Safe because superhero_basic is expected to be also one-row-per-superhero; joining preserves one row per superhero. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., hero_power_link, which links heroes to multiple powers) without aggregation or distincting first, because that will multiply superhero_core rows and duplicate height_cm/weight_kg if treated as measures. Instead: aggregate the many-side first (e.g., counts of powers per hero from hero_power_link or an array_agg of power ids) to one row per hero, then join on superhero_core.id. | When composing metrics that sum or average physical attributes (height_cm, weight_kg) across sets of heroes, perform aggregation at the query level after any joins that expand rows, or use superhero_core as the pre-aggregated one-row-per-hero input to avoid double-counting. | If you must join to hero_power_link to compute measures like number_of_powers, do a left join from a subquery that aggregates hero_power_link by hero_id (e.g., SELECT hero_id, count(*) AS num_powers FROM hero_power_link GROUP BY hero_id) ON superhero_core.id = hero_id — this preserves cardinality and prevents duplication of superhero_core attributes. | Avoid joining to any table with possible multiple matching rows per superhero (events, appearances, relationships) without first reducing that table to one row per hero or using windowing/aggregation; otherwise height_cm and weight_kg should be treated as attributes, not additive metrics, to prevent semantic errors.

views.name: colour_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  colour
FROM colour

params.description: Lookup of colour names by id — answers questions about the canonical colour string for a given colour id.
params.when_to_use: Resolve or display the human-readable colour for a given colour.id | Compose into larger queries when you need to annotate rows with colour.name by joining on id | Filter or group results by colour when colour is a dimension (not an aggregated metric)
params.output_schema: id: the unique identifier for the colour, derived directly from the base table column colour.id | colour: the human-readable colour string/name, derived directly from the base table column colour.colour
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view; all outputs are direct base columns (no aggregates or expressions). If you need a metric, compute it in a composing query (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY colour.id) rather than expecting it here.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or many-side tables/views on colour.id — safe to join because this view is one-row-per-id and thus does NOT duplicate its own columns. Example: JOIN fact_table ON fact_table.colour_id = colour_lookup.id — safe because colour_lookup has at most one row per id. | Do NOT join to one-to-many dimension links without re-aggregating the many-side first; joining to a table that has multiple rows per colour.id (e.g., an events table keyed by colour_id) will multiply result rows and any aggregates computed after the join will need proper GROUP BY or aggregation to avoid double-counting. | Safe to join from other one-row-per-key dimension/lookups: e.g., join superhero_basic or superpower_lookup on their colour id columns if those views are also one-row-per-key — ensure the sibling view's grain is one-row-per-key before assuming safety. | Do NOT assume safety when joining to JOIN-type sibling views that represent many-to-many links (e.g., hero_power_link, hero_power_link_4) unless you aggregate the link table first — those joins are one-to-many or many-to-many and will duplicate colour_lookup rows and any measures derived after the join.

params.description: Provides the canonical mapping of colour id to its colour name — answers lookups of a colour's name by id and can serve as a dimension for reporting.
params.when_to_use: Lookup a colour name given a colour id (e.g., show colour for a record that references colour.id). | Join as a dimension to enrich fact rows with human-readable colour names. | Compose into higher-level views that aggregate facts by colour (when joined correctly). | Serve as the de-duplicated dimension for colour in report builders and SQL composition.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for a colour — derives from base table column colour.id | colour: human-readable name/value of the colour — derives from base table column colour.colour
params.metric: No aggregation metrics are defined in this view. Both output columns are direct passthroughs from base table columns: | id = colour.id | colour = colour.colour
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables or other views on colour.id (e.g., JOIN colour_lookup_6 cl ON fact.colour_id = cl.id) — safe because colour_lookup_6 is one-row-per-id (the view's declared grain is ['id']), so joining on id will not duplicate the colour dimension rows. | You may join this view to other one-row-per-id dimension views (for the same id) safely (e.g., if there is another colour-normalized view that is also one-row-per-id), because both are unique on id. | Do NOT join colour_lookup_6 directly to one-to-many child tables or join results that expand colour rows (for example, a table of events per colour that contains multiple rows per colour) without either: 1) joining the child to facts first (so the fact rows carry multiplicity) or 2) aggregating the child to one row per colour before joining. Otherwise the implicit measures derived from a downstream query (counts, sums) will be multiplied by the child rows and lead to incorrect totals. | If you need to build aggregate metrics at the colour level from a one-to-many table, perform aggregation on that table (e.g., SELECT colour_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM events GROUP BY colour_id) and then join the aggregated result to colour_lookup_6 on id — this pattern preserves correct cardinality and avoids duplicating the colour dimension's rows. | Because this view contains only base columns and no aggregates, it is safe to be treated as a dimension (non-measure) when composing: its values should not be summed; instead, aggregate from the fact side after joining.

views.name: superhero_with_colour_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id,
  s.superhero_name,
  ce.colour AS eye_colour_name,
  ch.colour AS hair_colour_name,
  cs.colour AS skin_colour_name
FROM superhero AS s
LEFT JOIN colour AS ce ON s.eye_colour_id = ce.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS ch ON s.hair_colour_id = ch.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS cs ON s.skin_colour_id = cs.id

params.description: Provides one row per superhero with human-readable colour names for eye, hair, and skin colours.
params.when_to_use: Look up a superhero's eye, hair, and skin colour names by superhero id or name. | Presenting superhero profile rows enriched with colour text labels. | Joining superhero identity information to other one-row-per-superhero facts (e.g., core attributes or aggregated metrics) without duplicating counts. | Composing into reports or dashboards that need colour labels alongside superhero-level metrics.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the superhero — derives from superhero.id | superhero_name: superhero's name/string label — derives from superhero.superhero_name | eye_colour_name: text name of the superhero's eye colour — derives from colour.colour joined as ce.colour on superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id | hair_colour_name: text name of the superhero's hair colour — derives from colour.colour joined as ch.colour on superhero.hair_colour_id = colour.id | skin_colour_name: text name of the superhero's skin colour — derives from colour.colour joined as cs.colour on superhero.skin_colour_id = colour.id
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.eye_colour_id | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | colour.id (as ce.id, ch.id, cs.id) | colour.colour (as ce.colour, ch.colour, cs.colour)
params.metric: No aggregated measures are defined in this view; all outputs are direct column projections/lookup values. | Derived columns are simple mappings: eye_colour_name = ce.colour, hair_colour_name = ch.colour, skin_colour_name = cs.colour
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to superhero_core (or superhero_basic / any other one-row-per-superhero normalized view) on superhero.id = <other_view>.id — safe because superhero_with_colour_names has one row per superhero.id so measures/rows will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to colour_lookup (or colour_lookup_6) on colour.id = <lookup>.id only when enriching the colour lookup itself; joining these lookup tables into this view is unnecessary because the colour names are already resolved here. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as hero_power_link or hero_power_link_4 without first aggregating the many-side (for example, counting powers per superhero) because those views contain multiple rows per superhero.id and would multiply rows from superhero_with_colour_names. Instead, aggregate hero_power_link into a one-row-per-superhero result (e.g., COUNT(*) AS power_count GROUP BY superhero_id) and then join on superhero.id to preserve correct cardinality. | If composing measures (counts, sums) from child tables: compute aggregates at the child side keyed by superhero.id, then join the aggregated result to this view on id. Example safe pattern: (SELECT superhero_id, COUNT(*) AS power_count FROM hero_power_link GROUP BY superhero_id) AS agg_powers JOIN superhero_with_colour_names ON agg_powers.superhero_id = superhero_with_colour_names.id — this prevents duplication. | Because this view uses LEFT JOIN to colour three times, missing colour ids yield NULL names. Joins that assume non-null colour rows should handle NULLs accordingly. | Avoid joining other multi-row dimensions directly without aggregation or deduplication (for example, a free-form notes table with multiple notes per superhero) because such joins will multiply the superhero rows and any derived counts/metrics unless the multi-row side is pre-aggregated or limited to one row per superhero.

views.description: Provides one row per superhero with human-readable colour names for eye, hair, and skin colours.

views.name: superhero_basic_8
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,

SELECT
  sb.id AS id,
  sb.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  sb.weight_kg AS weight_kg,
  AVG(sb.weight_kg) OVER () AS avg_weight_all_superheroes
FROM superhero_basic sb

params.description: Per-hero weights with the dataset-wide average weight included (one row per superhero).
params.when_to_use: Get a superhero's weight together with the overall average weight of all superheroes in the table. | Compare an individual superhero's weight to the overall average in reporting or dashboards. | Compose additional aggregations that need a stable one-row-per-hero input augmented with the global average (for example grouping heroes by category and computing relative differences to the global average).
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the superhero - derived from superhero_basic.id | superhero_name: display name of the superhero - derived from superhero_basic.superhero_name | weight_kg: the superhero's weight in kilograms (base attribute) - derived from superhero_basic.weight_kg | avg_weight_all_superheroes: the global average weight computed across all rows in superhero_basic (window AVG over entire table) - derived from AVG(superhero_basic.weight_kg) OVER ()
params.metric: avg_weight_all_superheroes = AVG(superhero_basic.weight_kg) OVER ()  -- window aggregate computed across all rows of superhero_basic | weight_kg = superhero_basic.weight_kg  -- base attribute, not aggregated
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-hero (or one-row-per-id) on superhero_basic.id (e.g., superhero_core if it has id as primary key) — safe because this view has one row per superhero id so joins on id preserve 1:1 and do not duplicate the view's measures. | It is safe to join to publisher_lookup or colour_lookup only when those lookups are joined through a single-valued foreign key on the hero id or when you first reduce them to one row per hero (e.g., if publisher_lookup is already one row per id). | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many table or view (for example hero_power_link or hero_power_link_4) without first aggregating the many-side to one row per superhero id. Such a direct join would multiply rows for a single hero and thus duplicate weight_kg and avg_weight_all_superheroes measures. | If you need to combine with a many-side (hero_power_link, hero_power_link_4, superhero_with_colour_names if it expands colors), either: (a) aggregate the many-side to one row per superhero.id (e.g., collect powers or count powers) and then join on id; or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate (e.g., AVG or SUM) at the desired grain. views.name: superhero_colour_equality_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sb.id AS id,
  sb.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  sb.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  sb.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  sb.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  sb.publisher_id AS publisher_id
FROM superhero_basic sb
WHERE sb.eye_colour_id = sb.hair_colour_id
  AND sb.hair_colour_id = sb.skin_colour_id

params.description: All superheroes whose eye, hair, and skin colour are the same (one-row-per-superhero matching that equality condition).
params.when_to_use: Find superheroes whose eye, hair, and skin colour are identical (cohort selection). | Filter or join this cohort into downstream analyses (counts, lists, or aggregations) where each superhero should be considered at most once. | Compose with dimension lookups (colour names, publisher info) to enrich the cohort without changing row multiplicity. | Create aggregated metrics about this cohort (counts by publisher, counts by colour) after safe grouping/aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the superhero (derived from superhero_basic.id) | superhero_name: the superhero's name (derived from superhero_basic.superhero_name) | eye_colour_id: foreign key id referencing the superhero's eye colour (derived from superhero_basic.eye_colour_id) | hair_colour_id: foreign key id referencing the superhero's hair colour (derived from superhero_basic.hair_colour_id) | skin_colour_id: foreign key id referencing the superhero's skin colour (derived from superhero_basic.skin_colour_id) | publisher_id: foreign key id referencing the superhero's publisher (derived from superhero_basic.publisher_id)
params.grounded_columns: superhero_basic.id | superhero_basic.superhero_name | superhero_basic.eye_colour_id | superhero_basic.hair_colour_id | superhero_basic.skin_colour_id | superhero_basic.publisher_id
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of superhero rows in this cohort (aggregate to be computed at query time) | distinct_superheroes = COUNT(DISTINCT id)  -- distinct superhero ids (should equal row_count because view is one-row-per-id) | cohort_flag = 1  -- implicit boolean/indicator that the superhero meets eye=hair=skin; implemented by the view's WHERE clause (not a stored column)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to colour_lookup on eye_colour_id = colour_lookup.id — safe because colour_lookup is a 1:1 (lookup) dimension and will not duplicate cohort rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to colour_lookup on hair_colour_id = colour_lookup.id — safe for the same reason as above (use separate aliases when joining multiple colour roles). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to colour_lookup on skin_colour_id = colour_lookup.id — safe for the same reason as above. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to publisher_lookup on publisher_id = publisher_lookup.id — safe because publisher_lookup is a 1:1 publisher dimension and will not duplicate rows. | DO NOT join directly to hero_power_link (or other one-to-many link/join tables such as hero_power_link_4) without aggregation because those are one-to-many from superhero -> powers and will multiply this view's rows (and thus multiply counts/metrics). If you need counts of powers per superhero, first aggregate hero_power_link to one row per superhero (e.g., COUNT(power_id) GROUP BY superhero_id) and then join that aggregated result to this view. | DO NOT join to any JOIN-type sibling views that introduce multiplicity (e.g., superhero_with_colour_names, superhero_with_publisher) unless you confirm they preserve one-row-per-superhero. Prefer joining base lookup dimensions directly or join pre-aggregated results. | When computing cohort-level aggregates (e.g., count by publisher or colour), group by the desired key from this view (publisher_id or a colour_id) and aggregate; this preserves correct counts because the view is one-row-per-superhero id. | If composing into a larger query with other superhero sources, ensure joins are on superhero_basic.id = other.id and that the other source is one-row-per-superhero (or is pre-aggregated) to avoid accidental row multiplication.
